mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the observed median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from the market mean at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases both interest rates and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
regime_hint: simultaneous monetary tightening and inflation acceleration
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, signaling uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.4% for five consecutive months signals strengthening household purchasing power, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 95% confidence.
